papers.title: Machine Learning Framework for Integration of Video and EEG Reveals Distinct Seizure Phenotypes in Mouse Models of Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Video-electrocorticogram (VEEG) recordings are the gold-standard diagnostic tool for detecting and characterizing seizures in rodent models of seizure and epilepsy. Manual/visual scoring remains the prevailing strategy despite significant limitations. Alternatively, automated and semi-automated analyses have been applied to either EEG or video features alone but integrating these disparate data forms presents a challenge that has not been sufficiently addressed. Here, we introduce an integrated machine learning pipeline that jointly leverages EEG and behavioral video data to enable scalable and objective event classification. Integrated video-EEG analysis was initially validated using a well-established pharmacologically induced seizure paradigm in male mice, where overt generalized motor seizures provide a clear benchmark. We then tested the pipeline on a genetic mouse model of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) that displays a complex spike-wave discharge (SWD) seizure phenotype that poses significant challenges for traditional scoring methods. Machine learning-powered integrated analysis of video-EEG recordings outperformed unimodal EEG- or video-based approaches and performed favorably to experienced rodent EEG electrophysiologists while also uncovering distinct phenotypic relationships, including classes of atypical behavioral and typical non-behavioral SWD events. This framework provides a flexible tool for high-throughput, precise analysis of VEEG data, with potential to accelerate discovery in epilepsy and seizure research. Furthermore, this approach represents a generalizable strategy for the integration of diverse neurobehavioral time series data types.Significance Statement Seizure detection in animal models of epilepsy has relied heavily on manual analysis of video-EEG recordings, a process that is slow and subjective. We present a machine learning pipeline that integrates EEG and video data from mice to classify seizures with high accuracy. This work was validated across two models, first a pharmacologically induced generalized seizure model, and second, a spontaneous spike-wave discharge (SWD) model in genetic epilepsy. Our approach detected events missed by human reviewers and revealed previously uncharacterized SWD subtypes distinguished by their behavior. By combining open-source tools in a flexible framework, this work lowers the barrier to high-throughput, unbiased seizure phenotyping, and also offers a broadly applicable strategy for linking neural activity to behavior in neuroscience research.

papers.title: Window leakage in clinical EEG machine learning: matched subject-independent evaluation across ADHD and Parkinson cohorts.
papers.abstract: Windowed electroencephalography (EEG) pipelines can produce misleadingly high performance when segments from the same participant occur in both training and testing. We define this contamination as window leakage and test it in two clinically and technically distinct public cohorts: 121 children (61 attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder [ADHD], 60 controls) and 149 adults (100 Parkinson's disease, 49 controls). Signals were harmonized to 18 common channels and 128 Hz. All primary models used stratified 8-fold participant-disjoint evaluation, 50%-overlapping windows, participant-level probability aggregation, and validation participants drawn exclusively from each outer-training fold. A deliberately contaminated Random Forest audit contrasted random-window and participant-disjoint splitting. Random-window balanced accuracy reached 95.59% in ADHD and 92.02% in Parkinson's, but fell to 60.98% and 56.17%, respectively, when participants were held out. Thus, the inflation replicated across disorders, ages, recording tasks, and acquisition systems. Under correct evaluation, CNN-LSTM achieved the highest ADHD subject-level balanced accuracy (73.21%), whereas EEGNet achieved the highest Parkinson's balanced accuracy (63.75%). No architecture comparison remained significant after Bonferroni correction. One-, 2-, 4-, and 8-s windows produced no consistent cross-cohort ranking. Removing ATCNN-SA components also yielded dataset-dependent changes, and no ablation difference was significant after correction. Participant-bootstrap intervals remained wide despite tens of thousands of windows, indicating that inferential precision was governed by participant count rather than segment count. Window-level random splits contaminate clinical EEG performance estimates and must not be used to claim generalization to unseen individuals. Participants should be separated before model fitting, results should be reported at subject level, and split, windowing, aggregation, and uncertainty procedures should be disclosed explicitly.

papers.title: Stimulus overlap confounds generalization in EEG foundation-model benchmarks
papers.abstract: Neural decoding benchmarks commonly evaluate generalization across participants while reusing the same experimental stimuli in training and test sets. This design cannot distinguish transfer to new stimuli from recognition of familiar material, a distinction that is increasingly important for electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models, pretrained models designed to learn reusable neural representations. Here we introduce a training-matched audit that varies stimulus overlap while holding test trials, training participants and stimulus counts fixed. Across ten tasks from seven EEG emotion datasets, stimulus overlap increased differential-entropy decoding accuracy in every task and accounted for 77% of above-chance seen-stimulus performance on FACED-9. Across representations, overlap-dependent gains tracked stimulus identifiability; for CBraMod and LaBraM, advantages over input-matched handcrafted features were concentrated on familiar stimuli. Architecture-matched random controls nevertheless showed transferable benefits of pretraining on unseen stimuli. These results separate participant generalization from stimulus generalization and provide a framework for evaluating both in neural decoding benchmarks.

papers.title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection
papers.abstract: Asynchronous EEG event detection supports practical brain-computer interfaces by identifying event classes and temporal boundaries directly from continuous recordings without predefined event boundaries at inference time. The primary challenge lies in extracting event-related patterns embedded in ongoing background activity. To address this, we propose \textbf{NeuroDETR}, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework that combines structured tokenization with event-aware feature refinement. Multiscale temporal codebooks capture brief responses and sustained dynamics, while Spatial-Pyramid VQ hierarchically encodes spatial structure across EEG channels. These complementary representations form a compact event memory for jointly classifying events and estimating their onsets and offsets. Before tokenization, we apply FOCAL, an event-aware sparse attention module that uses predicted event presence to guide temporal feature refinement and spatial aggregation, emphasizing likely event periods while preserving context across the recording. Experiments on eight EEG datasets that span diverse paradigms demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. These findings provide a basis for the development of BCI systems that recognize meaningful neural activity during continuous interaction and monitoring.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Fatigue Detection from EEG Signals: A Methodological Pilot Framework with Potential for Nursing Applications.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is a significant occupational health issue that adversely affects attention and decision-making. This study aimed to objectively predict fatigue levels using EEG signals and machine learning models and to develop a physiologically based assessment framework with potential future applications in nursing. Time-domain, frequency-domain, entropy, Hjorth, and wavelet features were extracted from EEG data collected from 12 participants aged 21-40 years, with fatigue levels labeled using various scales. Classification performance varied across validation strategies. Under 5-fold cross-validation, Random Forest achieved the highest performance (accuracy=1.00, macro-F1=1.00), while KNN and NB also demonstrated strong performance. However, under LOOCV, sensitivity, precision, and macro-F1 values decreased despite relatively high accuracy. LOSO validation yielded more balanced results, with Random Forest maintaining the best performance (accuracy=0.97, macro-F1=0.91). EEG-derived features provide valuable information for fatigue assessment. Although high performance was achieved under certain validation strategies, subject-independent evaluation revealed more realistic performance levels. The proposed framework offers a practical approach to fatigue monitoring. Future studies should focus on larger, domain-specific datasets and multimodal integration to enhance generalizability.

papers.title: Symptoms of anxiety are linked to N3 sleep and lower dissipation of slow-wave activity during nocturnal sleep.
papers.abstract: Slow-wave sleep (SWS) is vital for brain health, memory, and emotional resilience. Slow-wave activity (SWA) reflects homeostatic sleep pressure, which dissipates across successive sleep cycles. Impaired SWA dissipation has been linked to depression. We examined whether reduced SWA dissipation is associated with symptoms of anxiety and depression in healthy conscripts. Seventy conscripts (67 males, aged 18-24) undergoing compulsory military service participated in overnight polysomnography. SWA dissipation was assessed by comparing normalized delta (0.5-4.0 Hz) electroencephalogram power between first and third NREM sleep episodes. This was complemented by full spectral analysis of sleep stages. Psychological measures included Overall Anxiety Severity and Impairment Scale, Beck's Depression Inventory, and Epworth Sleepiness Scale. Conscripts with elevated anxiety (24%) exhibited weaker SWA dissipation and greater proportion of N3 sleep. Similarly, anxiety was negatively correlated with SWA dissipation and positively with proportion of N3. Additionally, conscripts with elevated anxiety but without elevated depressiveness had less REM sleep than those with both anxiety and depression, as well as those without symptoms. Findings related to sleepiness or depression without anxiety were limited. In full spectral analysis individuals with higher anxiety exhibited elevated alpha power during REM sleep, potentially reflecting cortical hyperarousal. Higher proportion of N3 sleep and lower SWA dissipation were associated with greater anxiety rather than depression. These findings highlight the importance of adequate SWS in emotion regulation. Impaired SWA dissipation may contribute to preservation of negative emotional memories during sleep. Another possibility is that hyperarousal increases need for recovery sleep.

papers.title: Robust Functional Ward's Linkages With Applications in EEG Data Clustering.
papers.abstract: This paper proposes two robust linkage criteria, termed functional Ward-type linkages, for hierarchical clustering of grouped functional data, where each clustering unit is represented by a set of curves. Ordinary Ward's linkage defines the cluster dissimilarity between two clusters as the increase in the sum of squared errors (SSE) upon merging, which can be interpreted graphically as an increase in within-cluster dispersion. Motivated by this principle, the proposed linkages measure the weighted increase in band width required to construct a common band containing the central representatives of two candidate clusters. To reduce the influence of outliers, the central curves are selected separately within each cluster by leveraging the magnitude-shape outlyingness measure and the modified band depth, respectively. Simulations and two EEG data analyses demonstrate the robustness and competitive performance of the proposed methods under a range of contamination settings.

papers.title: Near-Zero Creep Ionic Elastomer for Non-drifting Ear Electroencephalogram Signal Acquisition.
papers.abstract: Monitoring and identification of ear electroencephalogram (Ear-EEG) signals offer a promising non-invasive approach for tracking mental states. Compared to rigid metal electrodes, polymer electrodes possess flexibility, good biocompatibility, superior skin adhesion, and wearing comfort, however, their accuracy is often compromised by signal drift due to polymer creep under sustained strain. To address this, we introduce a molecular strategy that suppresses creep by compensating entropy loss through a designed intramolecular dihedral structure. The copolymer integrates two distinct crosslinks: flexible segments stabilized by electrostatic self-coordination, and a minority of rigid segments formed by covalent main-chain bridges. In-situ scattering and theoretical simulations confirm that the covalently bridged TAO segments adopt a rigid dihedral configuration, effectively restraining chain slippage and eradicating viscoelasticity. Concurrently, dynamic disulfide exchange further enhances network stability under deformation. This design yields the near-zero creep polyelectrolyte ionic elastomer, denoted as Poly(TA-co-TAT)-TAO, which demonstrates remarkable stretchability (>200%) and elasticity (hysteresis <7.5%, recovery >99% at 160% strain). Leveraging its persistent creep resistance (<0.4% over 12 hours), the resulting wearable EEG device enables reliable, long-term mental status monitoring in real-world settings.

The material shows over 200% stretchability, low hysteresis, over 99% recovery, and creep resistance below 0.4% over 12 hours, enabling reliable long-term mental status monitoring with a wearable ear-EEG device.

papers.title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study.
papers.abstract: The weighted rich-club coefficient tests whether a network's most strongly connected nodes are preferentially interconnected. Its interpretation depends on two often-implicit choices: how the randomised comparison networks are constructed, and whether the hubs are re-identified in each comparison network or held fixed at those of the observed network. When hubs are defined by connection strength, these choices change what the coefficient tests. We examined how these choices affect inference using resting-state EEG from 20 people with Alzheimer's disease and 20 controls. Holding the data fixed, we compared four analysis pipelines, crossing two ways of building the comparison networks (global weight reshuffle or strength-conditioned null) with the two hub choices, and ran a calibration study using data constructed to contain no preferential hub coupling beyond nodal strength. An apparent eyes-open group difference in rich-club organisation appeared only under the pipeline combining a global weight reshuffle with re-identified hubs. Under the empirical resampling ensemble, that pipeline reported a group difference in 43% of pseudo-studies, always higher in the Alzheimer's disease group, while the other three stayed near the expected 5%. Unlike global weight reshuffling, strength-conditioned nulls approximately preserve nodal strengths; fixing observed hubs also retains the identity of the core being tested. The same data can support or dissolve an apparent rich-club difference depending on these choices. No single choice is universally correct, but reporting which were made, and why they fit the question being asked, is essential to interpreting the result.

papers.title: Paintable In Situ Gelling Bioelectronic Interfaces for Epidermal Electrophysiological Monitoring.
papers.abstract: Noninvasive epidermal electrophysiological monitoring is frequently constrained by unstable electrode-skin contact interfaces over soft, textured, and dynamically deforming skin. The predefined geometries of conventional electrodes limit their capacity to conform to local microtopography. Here, we introduce an in situ gelation strategy performed directly on the epidermis to construct a conformal ionic bioelectronic interface. A fluidic precursor comprising gelatin and tannic acid is initially stabilized against premature gelation via competitive solvent-solute interactions. Upon application, solvent evaporation and gelatin reassembly induce rapid network formation. This process directly yields a highly conformal and gently detachable interface with remarkably low contact impedance. The resulting hydrated dynamic network provides mechanical compliance, robust interfacial adhesion, stretch-tolerant ionic conduction, and cooling-induced interfacial weakening that enables gentle removal. The on-skin-gelled interface reduces skin-electrode contact impedance to 30 kΩ at 10 Hz, compared with 191 kΩ for commercial conductive pastes, and increases the signal-to-noise ratio from 24.9 to 27.8 dB. In proof-of-concept demonstrations, the interface supports within-subject electromyography-based gesture recognition with a classification accuracy of 93.4% and electroencephalography recordings of eye-state-dependent α-rhythm modulation as well as short-term sleep-related waveforms. These findings underscore the potential of on-skin in situ gelation as a versatile approach to fabricating paintable ionic bioelectronic interfaces for advanced electrophysiological monitoring.

papers.title: Multimodal neuroimaging and electrophysiological signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment with different amyloid-β deposition status: correlations with cognitive function and diagnostic value.
papers.abstract: Amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) is a heterogeneous transitional cognitive state between normal aging and dementia. Aβ positivity elevates dementia conversion risk but does not equate to prodromal Alzheimer's disease (AD), and not all Aβ-positive aMCI individuals progress to clinical AD dementia. Distinguishing Aβ-positive from Aβ-negative aMCI facilitates pathological subtyping rather than definitive early AD diagnosis. This cross-sectional study aimed to characterize scalp-level resting-state EEG and structural MRI signatures specific to Aβ-positive aMCI, explore their covariate-adjusted correlations with cognitive performance and regional Aβ burden, and develop an internally validated multimodal auxiliary classification model for Aβ stratification. Fifty enrolled aMCI participants (30 Aβ-positive, 20 Aβ-negative) and 35 cognitively normal controls (NC) completed unified 20-min eyes-closed resting-state scalp EEG, 3.0 T structural MRI, 18F-AV45 amyloid PET and 18F-FDG cerebral metabolism PET examinations. Artifact-free scalp EEG spectral power and regional θ/α ratio were calculated via Welch spectral analysis; voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was adopted to quantify whole-brain gray matter volume. Covariate-controlled partial correlation corrected for multiple comparisons was applied to evaluate cross-modal associations among cortical Aβ SUVR load, cerebral glucose metabolism and domain-specific cognitive scores. A binary logistic regression classification model combining screened EEG and MRI markers was established, with DeLong test for ROC curve comparison and 1,000-bootstrap internal validation. (1) Relative to Aβ-negative aMCI and NC groups, the Aβ-positive subgroup presented significantly elevated whole-scalp θ relative power and scalp θ/α ratio, decreased scalp α and β relative power (all q < 0.05, FDR-corrected), with predominant scalp oscillatory alterations distributed over temporal, parietal and occipital scalp electrode clusters. The temporal scalp θ/α ratio yielded optimal classification performance for Aβ stratification (AUC = 0.875). (2) The Aβ-positive subgroup showed significant gray matter atrophy across 13 AD-vulnerable brain regions including bilateral fusiform gyrus, inferior parietal lobule, parahippocampal gyrus, precuneus and right entorhinal cortex (all q < 0.05), with the maximum effect size identified in the right precuneus (partial η 2 = 0.477, AUC = 0.778). (3) Within the Aβ-positive subgroup, the temporal scalp θ/α ratio was positively correlated with medial temporal Aβ SUVR (r = 0.501, 95% CI [0.146, 0.732], q = 0.030); right precuneus gray matter volume was negatively correlated with multi-region cortical Aβ burden (q < 0.05). Left parahippocampal gyrus volume was positively correlated with MoCA memory subscores (r = 0.479, 95% CI [0.118, 0.709], q < 0.05). No significant associations between scalp EEG metrics and FDG glucose metabolism survived FDR correction. (4) The multimodal logistic regression model integrating temporal scalp θ/α ratio and right precuneus gray matter volume achieved favorable classification efficacy for Aβ-positive aMCI differentiation (AUC = 0.852, 95% CI [0.748, 0.955]), with good calibration and clinical net benefit based solely on internal bootstrap validation. The temporal scalp θ/α ratio and right precuneus gray matter volume are promising candidate non-invasive auxiliary biomarkers for Aβ pathological stratification in aMCI, rather than validated clinical diagnostic biomarkers. The multimodal model provides supplementary subtyping value within this single-center cohort, while external multicenter validation is mandatory before clinical application. This cross-sectional dataset cannot support prediction of longitudinal progression to AD dementia.

papers.title: Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure.
papers.abstract: Irritability is characterized by a propensity to experience frustration and has been associated with reduced self-reported willingness to expend effort for rewards. Frustration may be relevant to effortful reward pursuit, but its effects on effort expenditure have rarely been experimentally tested in humans. To address this gap, this study introduced a frustration induction in the Effort-Doors task to elicit frustrative nonreward (FNR), a negative emotional state triggered by unexpected reward loss, and examined its effects on physical effort expenditure and feedback-related electroencephalographic (EEG) activity. We also tested whether these effects vary as a function of state and trait measures of motivation and affect. Linear mixed-effects models tested the effects of FNR induction on self-reported, behavioral, and EEG measures in young adults (N = 83) completing the Frustrative Effort-Doors task. Models tested manipulation effects, trial-level post-feedback adjustment, and moderation by state and trait measures. Midfrontal theta power (MFθ) extracted using multivariate spatial filtering was examined as a function of feedback (win vs. FNR), effort (low vs. high), and subsequent behavioral adjustments. The frustration condition was associated with decreased self-reported state motivation and increased frustration, arousal, and response speed. Midfrontal theta power was larger following FNR feedback and increased with state frustration during high-effort trials. Higher state frustration was associated with reduced response vigor during effort execution following FNR feedback. MFθ did not predict trial-to-trial behavioral adjustments. These findings indicate that FNR recruits MFθ, a neural marker of cognitive control, while state frustration modulates physical effort execution following unexpected reward loss.

papers.title: In-laboratory polysomnography as the reference standard in sleep research: a bibliometric overview of human studies.
papers.abstract: In-laboratory attended Polysomnography (PSG) is the reference standard for objective sleep assessment. Although portable and wearable sleep technologies have advanced, the evolution of PSG research over the past decade has not been systematically characterized. Bibliometric data from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015-2025) were retrieved using a search strategy focused on in-laboratory, full-night PSG studies, yielding 462 publications for analysis. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Microsoft Excel were used to conduct visual and quantitative analyses of publication trends, country- and institution-level co-authorship, journal distribution, author keywords, and keywords bursts. Annual publications exhibited a steady increase, with the United States and China as the leading contributors. Prominent institutions included Eindhoven University of Technology and Seoul National University. PSG research was predominantly published in specialized sleep medicine journals. Keyword analysis revealed a stable thematic core encompassing sleep monitoring, sleep staging, and sleep apnea, alongside emerging trends in machine learning, wearable devices, and brain modeling. Within the corpus of included in-laboratory PSG studies, research outputs demonstrated a sustained trajectory, exhibiting a pattern of parallel development between clinical applications and technical refinement. While PSG remains a foundational methodological pillar in this specific domain, its evolving integration with advanced computational methods underscores a continued commitment to bridging clinical relevance and technological progress within PSG-focused research.

papers.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
papers.abstract: Acute cognitive challenge produces consistent changes in several EEG indices, including alpha-band desynchronization, frontocentral theta enhancement, beta-band activity, and the theta/beta ratio. These measures serve as common biomarkers of cognitive workload and stress. It is not yet clear whether chronic occupational exposure to high cognitive demand alters these responses. Emergency physicians offer a useful test case, since their work involves repeated cognitive control under time pressure and high-stakes decision-making. We recorded 19-channel electroencephalography from 17 board-certified emergency physicians and 18 non-healthcare comparison participants during eyes-open rest and a standardized composite challenge combining Stroop interference, serial subtraction, time pressure, and evaluative feedback. Spectral power was estimated with Welch's method, log-transformed, and analyzed using a hierarchical framework combining six a priori regional features with electrode-wise topographic mapping. Across groups, the challenge produced robust frontal and posterior alpha suppression and increased frontocentral theta, consistent with workload-related cortical engagement. No Group x Condition interaction survived false discovery rate correction for the regional features, and no exploratory electrode-wise interaction survived correction across the full feature set. A complementary Bayesian analysis yielded moderate evidence for the null for the alpha and theta features, but inconclusive evidence for the beta and theta/beta features. Sub-band decomposition showed the challenge-related beta increase was specific to high beta (20-30 Hz), while low and mid beta decreased in emergency physicians. These results indicate an absence of detectable large group differences in EEG stress biomarkers following prolonged occupational exposure to high cognitive demand, although the sample constrains this conclusion to large effects.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine Inhibition of GABA Neurons in the Ventral Tegmental Area Attenuates the Depth of Sedation in Mice.
papers.abstract: Dexmedetomidine is a sedative anesthetic with a unique ability to produce an arousable state of sedation. However, the neural mechanisms underlying this arousable sedation remain incompletely understood. Previous studies have implicated dopaminergic neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA) in mediating this effect, but the upstream neural circuit mechanisms remain unclear. Furthermore, although VTA GABAergic neurons exert robust inhibitory effects on dopaminergic neurons, their specific role in dexmedetomidine-induced arousable sedation remains unclear. Vgat-Cre transgenic mice were used to investigate the role of VTA GABAergic neurons in dexmedetomidine-induced arousable sedation. Electroencephalography (EEG), fiber photometry, calcium imaging, GABA neurotransmitter sensing, chemogenetic manipulation, and immunohistochemistry were used to assess neuronal activity, GABAergic signaling, and behavioral responses to dexmedetomidine. Fiber photometry using the calcium indicator GCaMP6m revealed that dexmedetomidine inhibited VTA GABAergic neurons. Fiber photometry with the GABA neurotransmitter sensor iGABASnFR demonstrated that dexmedetomidine increased GABAergic input to VTA GABAergic neurons. Chemogenetic manipulation combined with EEG demonstrated that activating VTA GABAergic neurons deepened dexmedetomidine-induced sedation, whereas inhibiting these neurons attenuated sedation. These findings suggest that dexmedetomidine increases GABAergic input to VTA GABAergic neurons and suppresses their activity, potentially contributing to its arousable sedative effects. Further studies are needed to establish the causal role of this neural circuit mechanism.

papers.title: VAD-EmotionNet: a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in the 3D affective space.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals are of great significance in human-computer interaction and affective computing, as they can objectively reflect transient neural dynamics in the brain. However, existing methods still face several challenges, including limited training samples, susceptibility of EEG signals to noise interference, and insufficient granularity in conventional two-dimensional emotion models. To address these issues, this study proposes VAD-EmotionNet, an EEG-based emotion recognition model built upon the three-dimensional valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) emotional space. Specifically, the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) is employed to extract non-stationary differential entropy (DE) features for constructing volumetric spatial-spectral representations. Moreover, a multi-query spatial-spectral attention (MQSSA) network is introduced to constrain head-specific representational flexibility through shared key-value projections while modeling long-range spatial dependencies across EEG channels. In addition, a cosine temporal inference correction (CTIC) module is designed to optimize feature distributions on a hypersphere using supervised contrastive loss, thereby smoothing local prediction anomalies. The proposed model is evaluated on the DEAP and DREAMER benchmark datasets using leave-one-trial-out (LOTO) cross-validation. Experimental results demonstrate that VAD-EmotionNet achieves competitive performance across multiple classification tasks, highlighting its strong capability in decoding complex neural representations. These findings lay a solid foundation for the real-world application of emotion-aware systems within a 3D affective space.

papers.title: Characterization of the Bispectral Index in Healthy Volunteers Receiving Inhalation Anesthetics in Combination With Opioids in a Randomized Trial.
papers.abstract: Processed electroencephalogram (pEEG) monitors are commonly used in anesthesia practice. The relationship between the pEEG and clinical levels of sedation over anesthetic concentrations with and without opioids is not well understood. The purpose of this trial was to investigate the relationship between Bispectral IndexTM (BISTM), clinical measures of sedation, and inhaled anesthetics across a range of anesthetic concentrations and hypnotic states with and without intravenous opioids. This prospective, randomized trial enrolled 211 healthy volunteers. Participants were randomized to one of five anesthetic regimens: sevoflurane, sevoflurane with remifentanil, sevoflurane with fentanyl, desflurane, or isoflurane. Target anesthetic end-tidal concentrations were increased in a stepwise fashion until a BIS index of 30 to 40 was reached. Opioids were administered by target-controlled infusion and commenced before the inhaled agent began. At each targeted end-tidal concentration, responsiveness was assessed using the Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (MOAA/S) score and the BIS index was recorded. The MOAA/S score was used to assess participant responsiveness, with a score ≤2 considered unresponsive and a score ≥3 considered responsive. The primary outcome measure was the BIS50 for each anesthetic regimen, representing the BIS index at which 50% of participants were unresponsive. Secondary outcomes included BIS95 (representing the BIS index at which 95% of participants were unresponsive) and evaluation of the BIS index as a predictor of responsiveness. BIS50 and BIS95 were estimated using random intercept logistic regression models, and the predictive performance of BIS indices was assessed by calculating the corresponding area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). One hundred and forty-three participants were randomized to a treatment group and completed the procedure with adequate data. Mean age was 26.5 ± 6.7 years (52% male). There were no reported device-related adverse events. Across treatment groups, BIS50 ranged from 67.5 (95% confidence interval [CI], 63.6-71.4) to 76.2 (73.5-78.8), and BIS95 ranged from 49.1 (42.9-55.4) to 63.3 (59.5-67.2). Compared to the sevoflurane and isoflurane groups, the desflurane group exhibited slightly lower BIS50 and BIS95 values. The addition of opioids to sevoflurane had minimal impact on BIS50 and BIS95. The BIS index alone was a strong predictor of the level of responsiveness, with AUCs consistently close to the ideal value of 1 (≥0.95) across all treatment groups. BIS indices were highly correlated with MOAA/S scores. These results describe the relationship between BIS levels and responsiveness for commonly used volatile anesthetics, with and without opioids, across a range of anesthetic concentrations. The results of this study should be interpreted in light of the study design which included young, healthy adult volunteers with no sustained, noxious stimulation. These findings may not be generalizable to other populations or clinical situations.

papers.title: Differences in neurovascular coupling in patients with major depressive disorder: Evidence from simultaneous resting-state EEG-fNIRS.
papers.abstract: Neurovascular coupling (NVC), the relationship between neural activity and cerebral hemodynamic responses, remains poorly understood in major depressive disorder (MDD). To investigate alterations in NVC associated with depressive symptom severity, we simultaneously recorded resting-state electroencephalography (rsEEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in 206 participants, including 134 patients with MDD and 72 healthy controls stratified by age to disentangle disease-related alterations from age-associated effects. NVC in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) was characterized by the consistency and temporal lag between spontaneous electrophysiological peaks and corresponding hemodynamic responses. We found that age significantly enhances the NVC consistency (p < 0.05), whereas this relationship was altered in patients with MDD during both the oxygen-consumption phase and the subsequent hemodynamic compensation phase. Furthermore, among patients with MDD, the strength of this consistency decreased more significantly with greater illness severity (partial r = -0.336, p = 0.0601). These findings suggest that changes in neurovascular coupling effects are strongly associated with the severity of depression. By leveraging wearable neuroimaging techniques, this study provides multimodal evidence for altered neurovascular coupling in depression and highlights its potential as a biomarker for disease monitoring and recovery trajectories.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Microstate Dynamics and their Associations with Acclimatization Index and Serum Albumin in Healthy Adults with Chronic High-Altitude Exposure.
papers.abstract: High-altitude hypoxia has been examined with conventional electroencephalography (EEG), event-related potentials, and neuroimaging, but its association with millisecond-scale resting-state EEG microstate dynamics and peripheral physiology remains unclear. We studied healthy adults including 124 low-altitude (LA) participants (50 men, 74 women) and 174 high-altitude (HA) participants (42 men, 132 women; age 28.05 ± 8.59 years; age unavailable for LA). Coverage, duration, global explained variance (GEV), occurrence, and transition probabilities were extracted for four canonical microstates. LA-HA differences were tested using unadjusted linear models; within-HA associations among the high-altitude acclimatization index (AAI), serum albumin, and Microstate A-related indicators were examined using covariate-adjusted regressions and exploratory bootstrapped mediation analyses. Compared with LA participants, HA participants showed increased Microstate A duration and GEV, decreased occurrence, and unchanged coverage, together with reduced Microstate B-related indicators, enhanced Microstate C-related indicators, and increased A→B and A→C transitions. Within HA participants, AAI was negatively associated with serum albumin, and exploratory mediation analyses indicated indirect associations between AAI and Coverage A, Occurrence A, GEV A, and Microstate A-originating transitions through serum albumin. These findings suggest that chronic high-altitude exposure is associated with resting-state EEG microstate reorganization in healthy adults and that acclimatization-related individual differences may be linked to Microstate A dynamics through serum albumin-related peripheral status.

papers.title: Dynamic EEG network responses to acupuncture stimulation in patients with stroke: a neurophysiological study.
papers.abstract: Acupuncture may modulate brain activity through effects on the central nervous system. This study aimed to investigate short-term changes in spontaneous EEG activity and functional connectivity during acupuncture in patients with stroke using multichannel electroencephalography (EEG). Multichannel EEG recordings were collected at three stages: before acupuncture, during acupuncture, and after acupuncture. Acupuncture was applied at Jianyu, Quchi, and Waiguan. EEG activity was evaluated using power spectral density (PSD) analysis. Functional connectivity was assessed using the weighted phase lag index (wPLI). Functional brain networks were constructed for different frequency bands. Graph theory analysis was used to examine clustering coefficient and global efficiency across different network sparsities. Power spectral density analysis showed significant stage-related changes in delta, theta, and alpha relative power, but not in beta power. Delta relative power decreased during acupuncture and partially recovered after acupuncture, but remained comparable to the pre-acupuncture level. Theta relative power increased during acupuncture and then decreased after acupuncture, with the post-acupuncture level lower than the pre-acupuncture level. Alpha relative power increased during acupuncture and decreased after acupuncture, but remained higher than the pre-acupuncture level. Whole-brain average wPLI showed a decrease in the delta band and an increase in the alpha band during acupuncture. No significant stage-related changes were observed in the theta-band average wPLI after correction for multiple comparisons. Graph-theoretical measures, including clustering coefficient and global efficiency, did not show statistically significant stage-related changes at the selected sparsity. Acupuncture was associated with short-term, frequency-dependent changes in spontaneous EEG activity and functional connectivity in patients with stroke. The observed changes were mainly reflected in spectral power and whole-brain average wPLI, while changes in overall network topology were not statistically supported. These findings provide preliminary neurophysiological evidence for the brain response to acupuncture stimulation.

papers.title: Optimized hybrid Transformer-based model for EEG classification: application to wheelchair control.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to improve the classification of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals for motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs), thus enabling more reliable user interactions in assistive technologies such as autonomous wheelchairs. The study contributes by systematically investigating and comparing the performance of both simple (Transformer, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)) and hybrid deep learning architectures (Transformer + CNN, Transformer + LSTM, CNN + LSTM) for EEG signal classification using multiple evaluation metrics, including accuracy, ROC AUC, confusion matrices, and prediction time. The findings demonstrate that the Transformer + CNN hybrid model consistently outperforms all other architectures, thereby achieving perfect classification accuracy (1.00), zero misclassifications, flawless AUC scores (1.000), and a competitive inference time (1.17 s), thus making it highly suitable for real-time MI-BCI applications. In contrast, simple models, particularly LSTM, show lower accuracies and reduced stabilities. Overall, this study highlights the advantage of combining attention mechanisms and convolutional architectures to effectively capture both spatial and contextual patterns in nonstationary EEG signals, thus establishing Transformer-based hybrid models as a promising approach for robust, real-time EEG classifications in next-generation MI-BCI systems.

papers.title: Short-term subjective and EEG responses following cervical rotatory manipulation are not reproduced by simulated cracking sound: A randomized controlled study.
papers.abstract: Cervical rotatory manipulation (CRM) is commonly used for neck-related symptoms and is often accompanied by a cracking sound. Whether a simulated cracking sound can reproduce the short-term subjective and neurophysiological responses to the complete CRM remains unclear. This study compared short-term subjective and electroencephalography (EEG) responses to CRM with those following sham manipulation with or without a simulated cracking sound. In this randomized controlled trial with three parallel groups and a single intervention session, 54 healthy volunteers were allocated to CRM, sham manipulation, or sham + simulated sound. Positive affect, negative affect, comfort, satisfaction, and eyes closed resting state EEG were assessed before and after the intervention. Prespecified EEG derived outcomes included frontal alpha power, frontal alpha/beta ratio, occipital individual alpha frequency, and alpha band frontoparietal and frontotemporal functional connectivity. CRM produced greater improvements in positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction than sham manipulation or sham + simulated cracking sound, whereas no clear difference among groups was observed for negative affect. Differences among groups were also observed in frontal alpha/beta ratio and alpha band frontoparietal and frontotemporal functional connectivity. Sham + simulated sound did not reproduce the overall pattern of subjective and EEG responses observed after CRM. CRM produced greater improvements over the short-term in positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction and was accompanied by differences in selected resting state EEG outcomes compared with sham manipulation with or without simulated cracking sound. Adding simulated cracking sound to sham manipulation did not reproduce this pattern. Because CRM differed from the control conditions in several procedural components, the specific component or combination of components responsible for these differences could not be determined. The trial was registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (URL: https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn; ITMCTR2025001112).

papers.title: Neural dynamics of induced throat vibrations during vocal emotion recognition
papers.abstract: Despite a large literature on the psychological and brain mechanisms of emotional prosody perception, the perspective of embodied cognition on these mechanisms has been largely neglected. Here we investigated the influence of induced bodily vibrations near the vocal tract on the categorization of emotionally ambiguous vocalizations while acquiring event-related potentials (ERPs) through electroencephalography. Emotional voices were morphed between a fearful expression and the speakers identity-matching angry expression, creating blends of emotions in each voice. In line with our hypotheses, behavioral results revealed that induced vibrations biased the participants emotion categorizations. Namely, induced throat vibrations of anger shifted responses toward anger for the most ambiguous voices, while fear vibrations shifted responses toward fear for anger-leaning voices. ERPs indicated that both anger and fear vibrations modulated frontocentral amplitude from about 75 ms, with the sign of the effect depending on time bins and morphing levels. These modulations show that vibrations are registered from early stages of processing. Source reconstruction highlighted effects of vibration types in prefrontal, cingulate, parietal, and medial and lateral temporal cortices, and to a lesser extent in somatosensory and insular cortices. Our results suggest that voice-associated vibrations may contribute to vocal emotion processing through an embodied feedback mechanism.

papers.title: Multimodal Evidence for Large-scale Network Imbalance in Etomidate Use Disorder.
papers.abstract: Etomidate use disorder (EUD) is an escalating public health issue in East and Southeast Asia, yet its neuroimaging features remain poorly understood. This study used simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to examine multimodal functional connectivity alterations in individuals with EUD. A total of 54 individuals with EUD and 46 healthy controls (HCs) were recruited and underwent simultaneous resting-state EEG and fNIRS recordings. Psychological dimensions including impulsivity, aggression, and craving were evaluated using standardized and validated scales. Source-level EEG functional connectivity and fNIRS hemodynamic connectivity were analyzed to identify group differences. Associations between altered connectivity features and clinical measures were examined within the EUD group. Machine learning analyses were conducted as exploratory assessments of the discriminative information contained in multimodal connectivity features. In unadjusted exploratory analyses of BIS-11 and BPAQ subscales, the EUD group showed higher cognitive impulsivity, non-planning impulsivity, physical aggression, anger and self-directed aggression (t=2.32 to 4.54, p<0.05), but lower motor impulsivity, compared with HCs. Source-level EEG analysis revealed significant group differences only in the delta band, with reduced large-scale connectivity in EUD involving default mode, dorsal attention, visual and sensorimotor systems. fNIRS analysis showed reduced hemodynamic connectivity across multiple frontal subregions and motor-related areas. Weaker connectivity between the primary motor cortex and the triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus was associated with stronger negative reinforcement craving (rho=-0.471, p_FDR<0.05). Exploratory machine learning analysis showed preliminary discriminative performance, with the random forest model producing the numerically highest test-set AUC (0.80) in this particular data split. Convergent EEG-fNIRS findings suggest delta-band network decoupling and reduced frontal hemodynamic connectivity as multimodal neural features of EUD. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the neural mechanisms of EUD and may inform future objective assessment and treatment-monitoring studies.

papers.title: Inclusive electroencephalography practices for Black and Muslim participation in a White non-Muslim-majority country: A co-produced tutorial.
papers.abstract: Most electroencephalography (EEG) research is conducted in White-majority Western countries by White researchers. EEG practices therefore often explicitly and implicitly exclude minoritised groups, leading to low diversity in EEG data samples that deepens biases in interpretation and clinical utility. Because EEG electrodes must contact the scalp, Black people and Muslim women who wear a hijab (or, Hijabis) are two systematically excluded groups. As a group of EEG researchers, Black people, and Hijabis, here we describe co-produced practical approaches to overcoming EEG participation barriers, from recruitment to data collection, and provide co-produced text, photographs, and videos designed to break down these barriers. These approaches provide further tools for the EEG community to tackle systemic exclusion and foster better, more representative neuroscience.

papers.title: Associations Between Resting-State EEG Delta-band Activity at Selected Parietal Electrodes and Cognitive Changes Following Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.abstract: Transcutaneous auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (taVNS) may improve cognition in Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), but its electrophysiological correlates remain unclear. We explored whether parietal delta-band changes were associated with cognitive changes following taVNS. This exploratory secondary analysis included 26 participants with MCI from a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial (taVNS, n = 14; sham, n = 12) who had valid resting-state EEG data at baseline and Week 24. Absolute and relative 1-3 Hz delta power at Pz, P1, P2, and P5 were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA and EEG-cognitive correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Absolute delta power showed significant time effects at all four electrodes after FDR correction (all q = 0.008). Relative delta power at Pz showed an uncorrected group effect (F = 5.007, p = 0.035; q = 0.218). In the taVNS group, MoCA-B improvement was positively associated with relative delta-power changes at P1, P2, and P5 (r = 0.629-0.652, p = 0.012-0.016), whereas AVLTN7 improvement was negatively associated with absolute delta-power changes across Pz, P1, P2, and P5 (coefficients = -0.418 to -0.613, p = 0.020-0.048). Although these correlations did not reach statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons, they showed a relatively consistent direction across multiple electrodes. Relative and absolute delta power may reflect complementary aspects of spectral modulation. The convergent cross-electrode associations provide preliminary EEG evidence linked to cognitive response to taVNS. Parietal delta-band power may represent a candidate electrophysiological marker of cognitive change following taVNS in MCI. papers.title: Neurobiological mechanisms and brain network dysfunction in major depressive disorder: an integrative review.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent and disabling psychiatric disorder characterized by persistent mood disturbances, cognitive impairments, and significant systemic consequences. Despite its substantial clinical burden, diagnosis remains challenging because current approaches rely largely on subjective symptom-based assessments and are complicated by marked biological and clinical heterogeneity. In this review, we synthesize findings from neuroimaging, electrophysiology, genetics, and molecular studies to provide an integrated overview of the structural, functional, and neurobiological alterations that underlie MDD. We discuss abnormalities involving large-scale brain networks, neuroplasticity and stress-related pathways, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and neurotransmitter systems, together with their implications for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response. Collectively, current evidence implicates both molecular dysregulation and large-scale neural network dysfunction in MDD, although direct evidence linking alterations across these biological levels remains limited. Integrating multimodal biological and neuroimaging approaches may improve diagnostic precision, facilitate personalized therapeutic strategies, and advance the development of biologically informed psychiatry.

papers.title: A homozygous GABRA2 variant associated with infantile spasms evolving to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome alters receptor gating.
papers.abstract: Variants in GABAA receptor subunits are increasingly implicated in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. Although GABRA2 variants have been associated with early-onset epilepsy, the functional consequences of individual variants, particularly those located outside canonical ligand-binding and transmembrane pore-forming regions, remain incompletely understood. We identified a homozygous GABRA2p.A407K variant in a patient with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) evolving to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS). Functional effects were assessed using two-electrode voltage clamp in Xenopus laevis oocytes and whole-cell patch clamp recordings in HEK293T cells expressing α2β3γ2 GABAA receptors. A Gabra2p.A407K/A407K knock-in mouse model was generated to examine neuronal membrane properties, provoked seizure responses, and behavioral phenotypes. The p.A407K variant did not impair receptor trafficking but slowed receptor desensitization. In hippocampal slices from adult knock-in mice, CA1 pyramidal neurons exhibited a more depolarized resting membrane potential and were positioned closer to action potential threshold, while action potential threshold itself was unchanged. In a limited adult EEG cohort of Gabra2p.A407K/A407K mice, no spontaneous seizures or overt epileptiform activity were detected. However, mutant mice showed prolonged seizure duration following 6 Hz corneal stimulation. Behavioral analyses revealed increased locomotor activity and altered exploratory behavior. These findings show that a rare homozygous GABRA2 intracellular loop variant alters α2-containing GABAA receptor gating and produces measurable neuronal, behavioral, and provoked seizure-response effects in a knock-in mouse model. The model does not reproduce the full human developmental epileptic encephalopathy phenotype but supports the conclusion that p.A407K is functionally consequential and provides a platform for studying variant-specific effects of GABRA2 dysfunction.

papers.title: EEG Correlates of Verbal and Perceptual Reasoning

Overall, the results did not reveal any pattern of significant relationships between these EEG measures and the two psychometric tests. Since this study had only a small sample, heavily skewed towards the high-IQ end of the scale, no definitive conclusions about the EEG measures and verbal and perceptual reasoning can be drawn. Nevertheless, it reveals many opportunities for further research, and suggestions are made for progressing this topic in the future.

papers.title: Controlled deep breathing technique intervention effects on resting EEG, subjective psychological distress, and executive function performance in young adults.

Forty healthy adults (ages 18 to 40 years) were randomly assigned to an experimental (CDBT) or control (natural breathing) intervention group for 20 min. Resting-state quantitative EEG (qEEG) was recorded before and after the intervention under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Behavioral measures included assessments of subjective psychological distress and executive functioning. qEEG analyses during resting-state focused on alpha/beta power ratios at frontal and parietal electrodes. Results showed a significant increase in alpha/beta ratios in the experimental group compared with the control group, particularly during the eyes-closed condition and at parietal electrodes. The experimental group also showed significant reductions in psychological distress scores and improvements in executive functioning measures, whereas no significant changes were observed in the control group. These findings suggest that CDBT may modulate frontoparietal oscillatory dynamics associated with relaxed mental states and improved executive functioning, providing preliminary evidence that CDBT may influence emotional regulation and cognitive control in healthy adults.

Outcomes were assessed over time and analyzed for Group × Time interactions. The Group × Time interaction for the attention index was not significant. The findings provide preliminary evidence that a group-based multimodal art intervention may enhance aesthetic engagement, positive affect, psychological flourishing, and alpha-based relaxation among lonely university students, although attention-related EEG indices remained unchanged. Multimodal art programs may offer a feasible and accessible approach to supporting university students' well-being.

papers.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.
papers.abstract: Motor vehicle collisions (MVCs) are among the most common mechanisms of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), and a meaningful proportion of affected individuals develop persistent post-concussion syndrome (PPCS) characterized by prolonged multidomain dysfunction. Conventional neuroimaging frequently fails to capture the underlying pathophysiology, leaving clinicians without objective diagnostic evidence. We describe a 57-year-old woman who sustained mTBI in a rear-end MVC in March 2023. Head computed tomography (CT) performed at the emergency department and a subsequent brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were both unremarkable. Despite normal structural neuroimaging, comprehensive multimodal functional assessment identified functional abnormalities across eight domains: vestibular function (videonystagmography (VNG)), cortical electrophysiology (quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG)), pupillary autonomics (automated infrared pupillometry), postural stability (computerized dynamic posturography (CDP)), oculomotor control (saccadometry), cardiac autonomic regulation (24-h heart rate variability (HRV)), olfaction (University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT)), and computerized concussion assessment (C3 Logix). Standardized psychological assessments confirmed moderate depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) = 14), moderate anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) = 12), clinically significant post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms (PTSD Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) (PCL-5 = 38)), and substantial headache impact (Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) = 58). The patient underwent a 10-modality individualized rehabilitation program. Concussion Symptom Checklist (CSC) scores declined from 92 at initial presentation to 0 by July 2023 (17 weeks post-injury), with near-complete re-resolution to 8 by February 2024 following a transient stress-related exacerbation. When conventional neuroimaging is unremarkable, comprehensive multimodal functional testing may provide evidence consistent with mTBI pathophysiology and help guide targeted rehabilitation. This case illustrates the potential value of a systematic, multimodal approach in PPCS management, while acknowledging that definitive attribution of findings to the index injury is constrained by the single-case design and absence of a pre-injury functional baseline.

papers.title: Open-Loop Deep Brain Stimulation Versus Closed-Loop Responsive Neurostimulation in Drug-Resistant Bitemporal Epilepsy: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Drug-resistant bitemporal epilepsy presents a therapeutic challenge when resective surgery is not feasible due to bilateral seizure onset or eloquent cortex involvement. Neuromodulation has emerged as an alternative, with open-loop deep brain stimulation (DBS) and closed-loop responsive neurostimulation (RNS) as implantable strategies. Comparative indications for modality selection remain unclear. A narrative review of articles published from January 2007 to January 2026 was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE. Approximately 120 articles were screened, and 39 studies were included. Due to heterogeneity in study design, findings were synthesized qualitatively. Both DBS and RNS significantly reduce seizure frequency in drug-resistant bitemporal epilepsy, with a median seizure reduction of approximately 60% to 75%. Seizure freedom, however, remained limited, reflecting the palliative nature of these treatments. Open-loop anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) DBS provides network-level modulation with low maintenance, while hippocampal DBS offers localized temporal inhibition. Conversely, closed-loop RNS delivers adaptive focal stimulation via real-time sensing and yields chronic intracranial electroencephalogram data. While both modalities show comparable efficacy, RNS may be advantageous in focal or asymmetric bitemporal epilepsy. Cognitive outcomes were favorable for both techniques, with RNS demonstrating the prevention of memory and language decline. Both DBS and RNS are palliative neuromodulatory options for patients in whom resective surgery is not feasible. Treatment selection should be individualized based on seizure network characteristics, laterality, monitoring needs, participation capacity, and cognitive considerations. The primary goal is to reduce seizure frequency and improve quality of life rather than to achieve seizure freedom. Future multicenter studies and biomarker-driven strategies are needed to refine selection and improve long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Syndromic Autism in Helsmoortel-Van der Aa Syndrome: From Clinical Suspicion to Genetic Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Syndromic autism refers to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) occurring as part of an identifiable genetic syndrome. Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome (HVDAS/ADNP syndrome) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the ADNP gene. We report a 10-year-old boy with ASD and intellectual disability who exhibited delayed motor and language development, characteristic facial dysmorphism, early tooth eruption, endocrine abnormalities, electroencephalography (EEG) abnormalities, and urogenital findings. Following unremarkable karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic de novo frameshift variant, c.1239_1240del, p.(Gln414Valfs*25) in ADNP. This case emphasizes the importance of considering a syndromic etiology in children with ASD accompanied by developmental delay, dysmorphic features, neurological findings, or multisystem involvement, and supports comprehensive genetic evaluation when first-tier testing is unrevealing.

papers.title: Neurological Assessment Tools and Inflammatory Biomarkers for Predicting Cerebral Palsy in Neonatal HIE.
papers.abstract: To evaluate temporal changes in serum interleukin-40 (IL-40), hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), and procalcitonin (PCT) levels between early and post-rewarming measurements in neonates with moderate-to-severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) undergoing therapeutic hypothermia (TH), and to determine the prognostic value of these biomarkers together with the Hammersmith Neonatal Neurological Examination (HNNE), amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting cerebral palsy (CP). Thirty-five neonates with HIE treated with TH and 20 healthy term neonates were prospectively enrolled. Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels were measured before and after TH. Associations between biomarkers, HNNE, aEEG, MRI findings, and CP at follow-up were evaluated. Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels decreased significantly between the early and post-rewarming measurements (all p < 0.001). Although biomarker levels differed from controls, they were not associated with subsequent CP. In contrast, HNNE, aEEG, and MRI showed strong prognostic performance for subsequent CP among surviving infants. Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels showed significant temporal decreases between the early and post-rewarming measurements in neonates with HIE undergoing TH; however, these biomarkers did not predict subsequent CP among surviving infants. HNNE, aEEG, and MRI each demonstrated strong prognostic performance for subsequent CP when evaluated individually in this cohort.

papers.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise.
papers.abstract: AI-driven generative art is changing the scope of artistic creation, but the principles behind its aesthetics and the perception of its outcomes remain relatively unexplored, especially concerning culturally specific art forms. The present study investigates how viewers cognitively, affectively, and evaluatively process AI-generated Chinese ink paintings, and whether artistic expertise moderates these responses. We introduce the concept of expressive expansion as a viewer-perceived psychological effect - the tendency for AI-generated ink works to elicit higher ratings of expressiveness and dynamic tension than traditional counterparts - and examine its neural and behavioral correlates using a multimodal paradigm. Stimuli generated using a pre-trained Stable Diffusion architecture were assessed according to three aesthetic metrics along with traditional and digital non-AI artworks by 120 respondents equally split into professional artists and non-artists. Multidimensional measurement based on eye-tracking, semantic differential rating, and EEG showed that, under blind viewing conditions, AI-generated stimuli yielded significantly greater scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional and digital non-AI works, suggesting that they engaged broader attentional exploration and increased attentional engagement as indexed by implicit behavioral and neural measures. Professional and non-professional evaluators agreed on expressiveness evaluation scores but differed considerably in their cultural authenticity perception, suggesting a dissociation between aesthetic appeal and cultural validity. These findings are consistent with a dual-pathway interpretive framework in which perceptual-affective and cultural-evaluative responses can dissociate as a function of artistic expertise - an account advanced as consistent with the observed dissociation rather than as a mechanism established by the present data - and contribute to the emerging empirical literature on audience responses to AI-generated art in culturally specific domains. All conclusions are restricted to the selected stimulus sets under the present experimental conditions. The source code, LoRA model weights, and experimental datasets will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/15100376058/ink-painting-ai-expressive-expansion (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20540420).

papers.title: A comprehensive investigation into EEG spectral analysis for ADHD brain dominance.
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that significantly impacts the cognitive functions and behaviour of individuals. It is characterized by abnormal brain lateralization in key brain regions linked to attention and cognitive control. This study aimed to explore and analyze the brainwave patterns linked to left and right brain dominance in ADHD, ADHD subtype, and control group using electroencephalography (EEG) spectral features, which have not been investigated in prior studies. Our study examined variations in alpha, beta, theta, and other frequency bands between the brain's left and right hemispheres, employing methodologies like EEG recordings with topographical views and statistical tests. The Asymmetric Index findings suggest a differential power spectrum density (PSD) pattern in ADHD subjects, with a higher average PSD in the right brain (RB) during working states and in the left brain (LB) during resting states. In addition, our corroborative study also uncovered that in ADHD subjects, theta and alpha waves are more dominant in the left hemispheric region, irrespective of the task state, and theta waves are notably prominent in the frontal region. The results of our novel study, supported by statistical analyses and topographical views, not only enhance our understanding of ADHD but also open avenues for more targeted and effective approaches in diagnosing and understanding the neurobiological underpinnings of ADHD and its subtypes.

papers.title: An all-in-one analytical platform for rapid determination of toxic dyes in complex water by SERS and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Rapid and reliable determination of toxic dyes in complex aqueous environments remains challenging because matrix interference and complicated sample pretreatment often compromise analytical accuracy and practical applicability. Therefore, an integrated filtration-adsorption-SERS sensing platform coupled with one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) modeling was fabricated for rapid and quantitative detection of malachite green (MG) and methylene blue (MB) in complex water samples. Polypropylene filter cloth (PPFC) served as a porous fibrous support for sample filtration, while Ag nanoparticles (Ag NPs) were uniformly immobilized on the fiber surfaces via a seed-mediated in situ growth strategy to provide SERS-active sites. Activated carbon was incorporated into the PPFC/Ag filter configuration to provide adsorption of the target dyes during sample treatment. The resulting configuration integrates filtration, adsorption, and SERS detection within a common analytical workflow, while 1D-CNN modeling was employed for quantitative analysis of the acquired SERS spectra. Benefiting from the integrated filtration-adsorption configuration and porous fibrous architecture, the platform exhibited high signal uniformity and favorable analytical performance, with detection limits of 10-9 M for both MG and MB. Adsorption kinetic analysis demonstrated that dye removal followed the pseudo-second-order model, with equilibrium removal efficiencies of 99.7% for MB and 98.6% for MG. To improve quantitative reliability in complex matrices, a 1D-CNN model was employed for SERS spectral analysis, yielding high accuracy with R2 values of 0.992 and 0.982 for MB and MG, respectively, with low prediction errors. Furthermore, spiked Moyan Lake water samples showed recoveries of 98.14% and 96.37% for MB and MG, respectively, with RSD values of 4.53% and 4.91%, demonstrating satisfactory accuracy and precision in a real water matrix. By integrating these complementary functions within the same filtration configuration, the proposed platform establishes a continuous analytical workflow from sample filtration and adsorption to SERS detection and quantitative analysis. This integrated design simplifies the conventional multi-step procedure and provides a sensitive, reliable, and practical approach for rapid monitoring of trace organic dyes in complex water matrices.

papers.title: Possible Epstein-Barr virus-associated central nervous system involvement with reversible electroencephalographic abnormalities in a child: a case report.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated central nervous system (CNS) involvement in children is uncommon and may present with nonspecific neurological symptoms. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may remain normal, making diagnosis challenging. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) has emerged as a useful diagnostic tool, although positive EBV results require careful clinical interpretation. A previously healthy 5-year-old boy presented with fever (38.5 ℃), headache, dizziness, and nausea for 3 days without seizures, altered consciousness, focal neurological deficits, or ataxia. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers. Brain MRI was unremarkable. CSF examination revealed an opening pressure of 120 mmH2O and mild pleocytosis (13×106/L, 100% mononuclear cells), with normal glucose and protein levels. CSF tNGS detected EBV (24,002 sequence reads; estimated pathogen concentration <103 copies/mL), while no other pathogens were identified and autoimmune encephalitis antibodies were negative. Serum EBV DNA was positive, and EBV serology demonstrated viral capsid antigen (VCA)-IgM positivity during the acute phase followed by VCA-IgG seroconversion during recovery. Electroencephalography (EEG) showed sharp and sharp-slow wave discharges in the left parietal, occipital, and posterior temporal regions despite normal MRI. The patient received intravenous ganciclovir (10 mg/kg twice daily for 2 weeks) and empirical ceftriaxone for 4 days. Clinical symptoms resolved completely, follow-up EEG normalized, and no neurological sequelae were observed at 1-month follow-up. This case highlights that possible EBV-associated CNS involvement may occur in children despite normal brain MRI and only mild CSF abnormalities. The combination of CSF tNGS, dynamic EBV serology, EEG findings, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and clinical follow-up may facilitate diagnosis. Because EBV detected in CSF does not necessarily indicate causation, results should always be interpreted in the context of the overall clinical presentation.

papers.title: Excitation-contraction coupling plasticity is revealed upon RyR2 depletion in adult mouse ventricular myocytes
papers.abstract: Ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) is central to cardiac excitation-contraction coupling (ECC), translating electrical signals into sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca2+ release and mechanical contraction. Although constitutive deletion of RyR2 is lethal, adult hearts can withstand a significant reduction in RyR2 expression without overt ECC dysfunction. We hypothesized that ECC possesses intrinsic homeostatic plasticity that rapidly adapts to acute RyR2 loss to maintain cardiac performance. Using an adult tamoxifen-inducible RyR2 conditional knockout (RyR2cKO) mouse model, we evaluated cardiac structure, electrophysiology, and intracellular Ca2+ dynamics. RyR2cKO mice survived for weeks with <10% residual RyR2 protein expression. In vivo echocardiography and electrocardiography revealed normal cardiac structure and function. Confocal Ca2+ imaging in intact hearts and isolated ventricular myocytes showed preserved Ca2+ transient (CaT) amplitude but slower release kinetics and elevated SR load. Simultaneous patch-clamp and confocal Ca2+ imaging established that L-type Ca2+ current (ICa) and ECC gain were maintained in RyR2cKO myocytes. Expression of CaV1.2, NCX, and phospholamban remained unchanged, whereas SERCA2a, IP3 receptor, and VMP1 levels decreased. Pharmacological inhibition of IP3 receptors did not suppress CaT, ruling out alternative SR channel compensation. These findings reveal remarkable intrinsic ECC plasticity, where high RyR2 channel reserve, elevated SR Ca2+ load, and CaT autoregulation collectively maintain cardiac Ca2+ cycling and contractile function despite profound RyR2 depletion.
